about.title: About
about.intro: FINCLUDIA brings together online courses, a tutorial blog and business tools for freelancers and companies (sole traders, SMEs) on a single platform.
about.approachBody: Each course is organised into lessons, with progress tracking and a certificate issued once the completion conditions are met. Blog content is publicly accessible, with some of it reserved for premium accounts depending on the user's profile.
about.securityBody: Protecting accounts and content (videos, images, documents) is a priority: every access is checked, and reserved content is never readable without permission.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions

items.question: What account types exist?
items.answer: The platform manages several profiles (sole trader, SME, industrial SME, with more categories to be added later), each with a standard or premium access level.

items.question: What's the difference between a standard and a premium account?
items.answer: Your account's level determines which content and features you can access: some articles, courses or tools may be reserved for premium accounts.

items.question: Is the blog accessible without an account?
items.answer: Yes, the blog is publicly accessible. Courses and tools, on the other hand, require you to be logged in and depend on your access rights.

items.question: How does course certification work?
items.answer: A certificate is issued only once all of a course's completion conditions are met.

items.question: Are my content and media protected?
items.answer: Access to proprietary content (videos, images, documents) is checked every time it is opened. No web solution can fully prevent the copying of content that is displayed, but the platform strongly limits the possibilities for direct retrieval.

jobOffers.title: Compare job offers
jobOffers.intro: Two or three offers compared on what they really leave: the salary, what can be priced around it, and what the job costs.
jobOffers.disclaimer: An indicative comparison, from the amounts you enter. The commute is compared in minutes and is never turned into money.
jobOffers.scoreNote: The score is optional. It appears only if you give weights, and its method is shown with it.
jobOffers.nonMonetisableTitle: Benefits that cannot be priced, shown apart
jobOffers.formulaNote: Net economic value computed with formula {{formula}} of the specification.

results.coutMensuelAnnualise: Yearly costs brought back to the month
results.coutsEmploi: Monthly costs tied to the job

bankUsage.title: My account's fit to my usage
bankUsage.intro: Compare 2 or 3 accounts already public in the comparator on what you actually use: card, withdrawals, transfers, account fees.
bankUsage.disclaimer: An indicative comparison from the public data already shown in the comparator. No absolute "best": the score only appears if you give your own weights. Online payment has no column in the client's workbooks and is therefore not compared here.
bankUsage.noneAvailable: No account is documented in the comparator yet.
bankUsage.scoreNote: The score is optional. It appears only if you give weights, and its method is shown with it.
bankUsage.noOnlinePayment: "Online payment" is not part of this comparison: no bank in the client's workbook publishes a dedicated column for it.

explorer.title: Explorer
explorer.intro: Search a bank offer by need, type or provider, among the comparator's already public data.
explorer.disclaimer: A literal search, with no ranking and no eligibility claim: every result is a public offer from the comparator, exactly as the bank published it. Reserved to people aged 18 and over.
explorer.noResultsHint: Try another word, or another rubric.
explorer.typeToSearch: Type at least two characters, or choose a rubric, to start the search.
explorer.reservedToAdults: Explorer is reserved to people aged 18 and over. Your age bracket does not allow access.
explorer.neverEligibility: A result shown here is never a guarantee of eligibility: always check the exact conditions with the provider.

workshop.title: Simulation workshop
workshop.intro: One entry point for every calculator: search a type of simulation, run it, keep the scenario and compare two or three of them.
workshop.noScenario: No scenario kept yet. Run a simulation above, then give it a name.
workshop.compareHint: Pick two scenarios, three at most.
workshop.noScoreNote: No overall mark: there is no defensible way to weigh a living allowance against a number of months. The figures are shown side by side, for you to read.
workshop.versionChanged: Computed with {{formula}} version {{saved}}; the formula is now at version {{current}}.
workshop.stale: The saved parameters no longer match what this simulator accepts: the figures are not recomputed.

finCategories.title: My categories
finCategories.intro: Categories are how your income, spending, goals, assets and debts are sorted. The reference list below is the one from the FINCLUDIA specification; you can rename it, hide what does not concern you, and add your own.
finCategories.referenceNote: The standard reference is never changed: when you rename a standard category, FINCLUDIA records your own name for it and keeps the original name shown beside it. Nothing is erased either: a category you remove leaves the list and stays readable by whatever already used it.
finCategories.restored: Category put back in the list.

errors.labelTaken: You already have a category with that name in this family.

finOnboarding.intro: A few questions are enough for a first useful result. You can skip any of them, save, and come back later.
finOnboarding.skipNote: No question is required. "Skip" is an answer, and "Why this question?" explains what each one is for. You can leave halfway: whatever is saved is kept.
finOnboarding.confirmNeeded: One amount looks very far from the others: {{questions}}. Check it, or confirm it as it is — nothing is blocked.

calendar.noCancellation: Removing a recurrence stops tracking it in FINCLUDIA. It cancels no subscription: the platform never contacts a provider on your behalf.

calendar.noCandidate: No recurrence detected in your recent movements.
calendar.provisionsHelp: Money set aside for a dated expense. A provision never creates actual spending: it enters no total of what you have spent.

paper.title: Practice portfolio
paper.intro: To practise without risking a dinar.
paper.noExecution: Nothing is executed anywhere: no order is sent, and none of these figures enters your real patrimony.
paper.pricesAreYours: The prices used here are the ones you state yourself. The platform publishes no quote and no list of instruments: that data has to come from the client, and nothing is invented in the meantime.

paper.rebalanceHelp: Nothing has been executed. Each line is a trade you make yourself if you want to.

checks.netFlow: The month has a positive net flow
